items.item_text: California Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
Graduation from an accredited school of social work with a Master's degree in Social Work (MSW)
Must be able to master detailed and complex information regarding benefits and coordination of care
A minimum of three (3) years' recent experience in the field of Social  Work
Experience providing short-term, evidence-based psychotherapy
Extensive, broad-based clinical experience
Experience working in a healthcare setting
Experience in identifying and analyzing care/service needs for patients
Training and experience in evidence-based therapies (CBT, Behavioral Activation, Problem-Solving Therapy, and similar)

The Primary Care Behavioral Health Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) provides behavioral health services to adult patients ages 18 and older within UC Davis Health’s collaborative, integrated Primary Care model. As an integral member of the multidisciplinary healthcare team, the LCSW partners with Primary Care providers and other healthcare professionals to address the biopsychosocial needs of patients and integrate behavioral health support into their overall care.
15% - Communication/Collaboration/Teamwork

Using advanced clinical judgment and evidence-based practices, the LCSW provides psychosocial assessment, treatment planning, brief psychotherapy, care coordination, and connection to community resources for patients experiencing depression, anxiety, grief, adjustment-related concerns, and other behavioral health needs commonly addressed in the Primary Care setting. The LCSW advocates for patient self-determination, confidentiality, access to appropriate services and resources, and meaningful participation in decisions affecting their health and well-being while practicing in accordance with the professional ethics and values of social work.
5% - Professional Development

This hybrid position offers the opportunity to provide meaningful, patient-centered behavioral health care within a collaborative academic health system while contributing to the continued quality and effectiveness of integrated behavioral health services. On-site work is located near the UC Davis Health hospital campus in Sacramento. The role currently serves the adult population, with the potential to expand services to pediatric patients based on future Department needs.
Demonstrated ability to work on a multidisciplinary team
Must have solid psychosocial assessment skills
Must demonstrate ability to effectively and efficiently handle demanding workload involving multiple tasks
Excellent analytical, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills
Skills to perform in-depth chart analysis to provide accurate information in a concise, informative manner
Requires a high level of clinical judgment, problem-solving skills, creativity, organizational and priority-setting abilities, with excellent communication skills
Knowledge of care/services provided in differing levels of care in ambulatory and institutional settings
Knowledge of community resources
Knowledge of biopsychosocial and behavioral health treatment plans
Ability to work with all levels of staff, both inter- and intra-departmental, to create a cooperative relationship and positive working environment
Knowledge of legal requirements and guidelines for providing psychiatric services, including mental status exams, suicide risk assessments, 5150 applications, and mandated reporting requirements
